title: Tangent spaces, Lie algebras and rational actions
statement: *Tangent spaces and differentials.* Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let X=Spec A and Y=Spec B be finite-type affine k-schemes, let x in X(k), and let phi:X\to Y be a k-morphism. The tangent space is T_xX := T_{X/k,x} as defined in [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], using the dual-number ring [def-sc-dual-numbers]. For rational points, [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality] identifies T_xX canonically with Hom_k(m_x/m_x^2,k), and [lem-sc-rational-point-tangent-derivation-identification] identifies its vectors with k-derivations at x. The differential d phi_x is induced by the tangent-map construction of [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] (equivalently, under the preceding identification, the dual of the cotangent map); differentials compose. *Lie algebra of a matrix group.* Let V be a finite-dimensional k-vector space and let G be a finite-type closed subgroup scheme of GL(V). For a commutative k-algebra R, G(R) consists of matrices satisfying the defining equations. Define Lie(G) := T_{G/k,1}, identified with {X in End_k(V) | 1+epsilon X in G(k[epsilon]/epsilon^2)} via X \mapsto 1+epsilon X (and T_1 GL(V)=End_k(V)), using [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] and [def-sc-dual-numbers]. By [lem-wf-lie-algebra-derivation-bracket], Lie(G) is a subspace of End_k(V) closed under the commutator [X,Y]=XY-YX, hence a Lie algebra in the sense of [def-wf-lie-algebra] under this bracket. *Rational actions.* Let M be a finite-dimensional k-vector space. For a regular homomorphism r:G\to GL(M) as in [def-wf-algebraic-representations], its differential at 1 is the linear map dr:Lie(G)\to End_k(M) characterized by r(1+epsilon X)=1+epsilon dr(X) over k[epsilon]/epsilon^2; by [lem-wf-lie-algebra-derivation-bracket] it is a Lie representation of Lie(G) on M in the sense of [def-wf-lie-algebra], i.e. dr([X,Y])=dr(X)dr(Y)-dr(Y)dr(X). The adjoint action is Ad(g)X=gXg^{-1} for g in G(k); it preserves Lie(G), since g(1+epsilon X)g^{-1}=1+epsilon gXg^{-1} and conjugation by g preserves G. Its differential is ad(Y)X=[Y,X], since over k[epsilon]/epsilon^2 one has (1+epsilon Y)X(1+epsilon Y)^{-1}=X+epsilon(YX-XY). *Matrix group schemes and smoothness.* A finite-type matrix group scheme is a finite-type closed subgroup scheme of GL(V), possibly nonreduced, with multiplication and inversion restricting from GL(V). Regular local rings and regular schemes use [def-weil-regular-scheme], and smooth ring maps use [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. For a finite-type affine k-scheme over the perfect base field k, the regular-local-ring criterion and its equivalence with smoothness at a point are the content of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local], and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-separable-residue-smooth]. A smooth matrix group is smooth at every closed point.

external.place: (That this subspace is closed under the bracket, and that $dr$ below preserves brackets, is standard: compare Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), Chapter 10.) *Rational actions.* A *rational representation* of $G$ is a regular homomorphism $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(M)$, i.e. an algebraic-group module in the sense of [def-wf-algebraic-representations].
